general_model_conventions.nrtl: tau_ij(T) = c_ij + d_ij/T + e_ij*H(T) + f_ij*T + g_ij*T^2
general_model_conventions.uniquac: ln(tau_ij(T)) = a_ij + b_ij/T + c_ij*H(T) + d_ij*T + e_ij*T^2
general_model_conventions.component_order: Component 1 is the hydrocarbon; component 2 is water.
general_model_conventions.atmospheric_vlle_vapor_treatment: ideal vapor; phi_i = 1 for both components

fit_scope.high_temperature_extension_method: Geometric interpolation between water-in-n-hexane and water-in-n-octane correlations.
notes: The water-rich branch is constrained by evaluated n-heptane experimental data through the upper end of the fit.
The heptane-rich branch above approximately 318 K is constrained by neighboring-alkane interpolation rather than direct n-heptane measurements.
The interpolation was treated as soft pseudo-data rather than as experimental n-heptane measurements.
The neighboring-alkane interpolation agrees with direct n-heptane measurements within approximately 4% near 298 K and approximately 8% near 318 K.

temperature_dependence.equation: tau_ij(T) = c_ij + d_ij/T + e_ij*H(T) + f_ij*T + g_ij*T^2

notes: The modern measured organic-rich branch is reproduced extremely well.
The larger aqueous-branch error reflects substantial scatter and curvature in the dilute heptane-in-water measurements.
The pseudo-data MAPE measures reproduction of the hexane/octane interpolation and is not an experimental n-heptane error.

temperature_dependence.equation: ln(tau_ij(T)) = a_ij + b_ij/T + c_ij*H(T) + d_ij*T + e_ij*T^2

modern_water_in_heptane.source: Morgado et al., Fluid Phase Equilibria 503 (2020) 112322
quality_notes: More than 400 water-saturated n-heptane samples were analyzed.
Estimated intrinsic standard deviation was up to approximately 5%.

mutual_low_temperature_validation.source: Susilo, Lee and Englezos, Fluid Phase Equilibria 231 (2005) 20-26
mutual_low_temperature_validation.role: Independent mutual-solubility validation on both liquid branches
mutual_low_temperature_validation.reason: Useful independent data but visibly noisier than the modern Karl Fischer organic-rich measurements and evaluated aqueous data.

aqueous_branch.source: IUPAC-NIST Solubility Data Series / NIST SRD 106
notes: The evaluator identifies substantial scatter among historical measurements.
Modern GLC measurements on the aqueous branch were considered substantially more reliable than several older values.
Old high-temperature water-in-heptane measurements were not used to define the extended organic-rich branch.

high_temperature_heptane_rich_extension.role: Soft constraint on the otherwise unconstrained high-temperature water-in-heptane branch

thermodynamic_basis.title: Thermodynamic analysis of the mutual solubilities of normal alkanes and water
thermodynamic_basis.justification: Tsonopoulos found the heat of solution of water in C6-C8 normal alkanes to be nearly independent of temperature and carbon number and used interpolated heptane correlation parameters. Geometric interpolation of x is linear interpolation in ln(x), and therefore in the corresponding dilute-solution free energy.

notes: Water solubility in neighboring normal alkanes varies smoothly with carbon number.
The interpolation reproduces available n-heptane data near the top of the measured range reasonably well.
These values must not be labeled as direct n-heptane measurements.

downweighted_or_rejected_values: Clearly inconsistent or malformed low-temperature pressure entries

model_agreement_at_upper_limit.assessment: The neighbor constraint removes the severe high-temperature divergence seen in unconstrained fits.

model_selection.reason: NRTL is marginally tighter on the modern water-in-heptane data, while UNIQUAC is marginally tighter on the evaluated aqueous branch.

temperature_term_selection.H_term: retained and materially improves temperature curvature

limitations: The heptane-rich phase above approximately 318 K is not directly experimentally constrained.
The 333-413 K heptane-rich extension depends on smooth carbon-number interpolation between n-hexane and n-octane.
VLLE pressure and vapor composition provide only weak constraints on trace liquid mutual solubilities because both liquid phases are nearly pure in their major component.
The fit should not be presented as experimentally validated above 413 K.

notes: Direct octane-system information is available throughout essentially the entire fitted range.
No neighboring-alkane interpolation is required.
The final approximately 6 K below the three-phase critical endpoint develops critical scaling that ordinary smooth NRTL/UNIQUAC temperature functions do not reproduce accurately.

alpha.selection_note: alpha = 0.15 gave the best performance among the tested fixed values for the extended-temperature fit.

temperature_dependence.equation: tau_ij(T) = c_ij + d_ij/T + e_ij*H(T) + f_ij*T + g_ij*T^2

centered_equivalent.equation: tau_ij(T) = value_at_Tref + d*(1/T - 1/Tref) + e*H(T) + f*(T-Tref) + g*(T^2-Tref^2)

fit_metrics.basis: Reproduction of the selected smooth mutual-solubility reference curves over approximately 273-533 K.
fit_metrics.warning: These sub-percent-to-percent errors are errors against the selected smooth target curves, not against every individual literature point.

centered_equivalent.equation: ln(tau_ij(T)) = value_at_Tref + b*(1/T - 1/Tref) + c*H(T) + d*(T-Tref) + e*(T^2-Tref^2)

fit_metrics.basis: Reproduction of the selected smooth mutual-solubility reference curves over approximately 273-533 K.

primary_high_temperature_source.source: Heidman, Tsonopoulos, Brady and Wilson, AIChE Journal 31 (1985) 376-384
notes: Measurements extend from ordinary temperatures deep into the high-temperature three-phase region.
Reported replicate precision is approximately ±5%.

nist_iupac_evaluation.source: IUPAC-NIST Solubility Data Series / NIST SRD 106
role: Compilation of Heidman and earlier measurements
notes: Independent octane-in-water measurements exhibit appreciable scatter.
Price high-temperature values are systematically lower than Heidman values.

critical_endpoint_extrapolation.assessment: Outside the recommended ordinary NRTL/UNIQUAC fit range; critical scaling becomes dominant.

critical_temperature_scaling_check.method: Fit the critical-temperature parameter of a Heidman-style critical correlation using only pre-endpoint data.
critical_temperature_scaling_check.interpretation: The location of the critical endpoint is strongly supported by the precritical data. The near-endpoint error is therefore principally a functional-form problem, not uncertainty in Tc.

model_selection.reason: NRTL gives marginally lower overall wide-range error, but the difference is negligible compared with experimental scatter.

temperature_term_selection.constant_plus_1_over_T: clearly inadequate for the full range
temperature_term_selection.quadratic_T: meaningfully improves the fit near approximately 500-533 K
temperature_term_selection.higher_order_terms: not recommended because they would mostly fit literature scatter and still would not provide the correct critical asymptotic form

limitations: Individual literature measurements scatter substantially more than the fitted smooth-curve MAPE values.
The five-term interaction parameters are highly correlated and should not be interpreted individually as physical quantities.
The standard coefficient representation contains substantial cancellation; the centered equivalent is preferable for numerical inspection.
Predictions above approximately 533 K should be regarded as extrapolation.
Accurate behavior in the final few kelvin approaching 539.1 K requires a dedicated critical-region correlation or a suitable high-pressure EOS.

heptane_vs_octane: The octane fit has substantially stronger direct high-temperature experimental support.
The heptane fit is directly well constrained to approximately 318 K on the hydrocarbon-rich branch and extended to 413 K using neighboring-alkane interpolation.
The octane fit is directly constrained into the precritical region and can therefore be recommended to approximately 533 K.

For both systems, atmospheric heterogeneous-azeotrope behavior provides a useful independent validation of vapor pressure and vapor composition but only weakly constrains trace liquid mutual solubilities.
